headline: Ward 42's firsts and lasts measure the same thing, a downtown scored as a neighborhood.
summary:
Most of what this scorecard finds here, good and bad, is one fact seen from different angles. The ward is last in the city for sunlight in both seasons because its own towers cast the shade. It is first for walking and biking to work because a third of working residents live within blocks of the jobs. Rent is the highest in Chicago and so is reported income, and those are one observation rather than two, since the only people who live downtown are the ones who can pay for it. Even the chain-store share, worst in the city, follows from ground floors that rent at prices only national brands can carry.

The crash figure needs the same lens. The 216 pedestrians and cyclists struck here is the worst count of the fifty, but it counts everyone hit inside the ward, and these sidewalks carry the densest crowds in Chicago, most of them workers and visitors who live elsewhere. It measures how much walking happens here more than how dangerous any one walk is. The clearest genuine wins are the boring ones. Pothole and rodent complaints close faster here than anywhere else in the city, and that is service a resident actually feels.
reading_the_rankings: The income figure deserves the most suspicion, in both directions. It arrives apportioned from ZIP code areas that ignore ward lines, its own publisher rates it low confidence, and it is an average, which a handful of very large tax returns can move a long way. First place is probably real. The number itself is soft. The modeled measures deserve doubt for a different reason. They estimate what a ward with these demographics usually looks like, and no usual ward looks like this one, a place whose daytime population is many times the number of people who sleep here.

news.headline: Trump Tower On Obama Way? Chicago Considers Honorary Designation For Downtown Street
news.note: The ward's alderman proposed an honorary street sign for the stretch of Wabash Avenue that includes the block with Trump Tower, naming it after Barack Obama.

alderperson.name: Brendan Reilly

The homepage reads 'Alderman Reilly represents downtown's 42nd Ward, Chicago's Central Business District and home to 90,000 residents and over 10,000 business licenses,' and the About page reads 'Alderman Brendan Reilly has served as a member of the Chicago City Council since 2007 when he unseated a 36-year incumbent,' confirming the site is his.
